newsitem.title: MACAU: Typhoon causes air, sea traffic havoc in Macau.
newsitem.headline: Typhoon causes air, sea traffic havoc in Macau.

text.p: Macau braced on Saturday for one of the worst typhoons to hit for years, which has already caused disruption to air and sea traffic.
Macau hoisted typhoon signal number eight at 11 a.m. (0300 GMT), an hour before neighbouring Hong Kong issued the same warning signal, authorities there said.
Signal eight means that winds with speeds of 63 to 117 km an hour (40 to 74 mph) are expected.
The Portuguese-ruled territory's small international airport was shut due to the bad weather. Ferry service to Hong Kong and other south China cities have also been suspended.
Hong Kong's TVB news said minor flooding occurred in some areas of Macau.

The Hong Kong Observatory said Typhoon Victor was expected to make landfall near the Pearl River estuary at around midnight (1600 GMT). Hong Kong is located at the eastern edge of the estuary, while Macau is located at the western edge.
